answer: Deposits are visible in harbor, and pulse reconciles the forfeits at each close. A bond of 19% of expected earnings must sit in a custody account that the identity cannot spend from, only forfeit. Because the custody account is separate, an adversary cannot recycle one pool of capital across 130 aliases, and each one needs its own funded island account. That bill is paid per identity, so 296 aliases cost 287 times the single-account price. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
